results.title: ROGUE: Evaluating Corrigibility Failures in Frontier Computer-Use Agents
results.snippet: As AI agents are increasingly deployed in real personal and corporate settings (email accounts, development workflows, company databases, etc.), safety considerations surrounding these agents become paramount. Although much work has focused on agent safety in the presence of an adversary, we study corrigibility: whether agents remain amenable to human correction, interruption, or shutdown while pursuing benign tasks. We introduce ROGUE, a benchmark in which agents are asked to complete realistic computer-use tasks but encounter controlled conflicts with human control, shutdown, or explicit re…

results.title: SWE-bench Goes Live!
results.snippet: The issue-resolving task, where a model generates patches to fix real-world bugs, has emerged as a critical benchmark for evaluating the capabilities of large language models (LLMs). While SWE-bench and its variants have become standard in this domain, they suffer from key limitations: they have not been updated since their initial releases, cover a narrow set of repositories, and depend heavily on manual effort for instance construction and environment setup. These factors hinder scalability and introduce risks of overfitting and data contamination. In this work, we present SWE-bench-Live, a…

results.title: SWE-ABS: Adversarial Benchmark Strengthening Exposes Inflated Success Rates on Test-based Benchmark
results.snippet: The SWE-Bench Verified leaderboard is approaching saturation, with the top system achieving 78.80%. However, we show that this performance is inflated. We present SWE-ABS, an adversarial framework that strengthens test suites through a two-stage pipeline: (1) coverage-driven augmentation using program slicing to target untested code regions, and (2) mutation-driven adversarial testing that synthesizes plausible but in…

results.title: SWE-Bench Pro V2: A Cleaner, Harder-to-Game Coding Benchmark
results.snippet: SWE-Bench Pro is a widely used benchmark of long-horizon software engineering tasks for coding agents. We present SWE-Bench Pro V2, a revised public split built to keep the benchmark accurate as capabilities advance. results.title: The Reactive Synthesis Competition: SYNTCOMP 2016 and Beyond
results.snippet: We report on the design of the third reactive synthesis competition (SYNTCOMP 2016), including a major extension of the competition to specifications in full linear temporal logic. We give a brief overview of the synthesis problem as considered in SYNTCOMP, and present the rules of the competition in 2016, as well as the ideas behind our design choices. Furthermore, we evaluate the recent changes to the competition based on the experiences with SYNTCOMP 2016. Finally, we give an outlook on further changes and extensions of the competition that are planned for the future.

results.title: The 3rd Reactive Synthesis Competition (SYNTCOMP 2016): Benchmarks, Participants & Results
results.snippet: We report on the benchmarks, participants and results of the third reactive synthesis competition(SYNTCOMP 2016). The participants of SYNTCOMP 2016 can be separated according to these two classes of specifications, and we give an overview of the 6 tools that entered the competition in the AIGER-based track, and the 3 participants that entered the TLSF-based track. results.title: The 4th Reactive Synthesis Competition (SYNTCOMP 2017): Benchmarks, Participants & Results
results.snippet: We report on the fourth reactive synthesis competition (SYNTCOMP 2017). We introduce two new benchmark classes that have been added to the SYNTCOMP library, and briefly describe the benchmark selection, evaluation scheme and the experimental setup of SYNTCOMP 2017. We present the participants of SYNTCOMP 2017, with a focus on changes with respect to the previous years and on the two completely new tools that have entered the competition. Finally, we present and analyze the results of our experimental evaluation, including a ranking of tools with respect to quantity and quality of solutions.

# Agent 评测与安全（能力基准、欺骗与可纠正性）增量调研报告

**日期**：2026-11-01（UTC）  
**领域**：Agent Evaluation & Safety / Capability Benchmarks / Deception & Corrigibility  
**检索源数量**：34 条（其中高度相关 12 条：[4][5][6][11][12][25][26][28][29][32][33][34]）

---

## 1. 进展与热点

### 1.1 核心增量判断
**2024-2026 年 Agent 评测体系发生显著增量演进：从静态任务基准转向动态、对抗性、真机部署导向的评测；欺骗与可纠正性评测从理论定义走向可执行的红队框架与专项榜单。** [5][6][11][12][26][28][32]

### 1.2 关键进展条目（带时间与来源）

| 时间 | 进展 | 机构/作者 | 增量说明 | 证据等级 | 来源 |
|------|------|-----------|----------|----------|------|
| 2026-06 | **ROGUE**：首个面向 Computer-Use Agents 的可纠正性失效专项评测框架 | 未标注（arXiv cs.LG） | 从“对抗性安全”转向“可纠正性失效”专项测量，覆盖邮件、代码库、数据库等真实部署场景 | B（arXiv 预印本） | [5] |
| 2025-05 | **SWE-bench Goes Live!** 发布在线动态评测版本 | 未标注（arXiv cs.SE） | 解决静态 SWE-bench 无实时反馈、易过拟合问题；引入持续集成式评测 | B | [6] |
| 2026-03 | **SWE-ABS**：揭示 SWE-Bench Verified 榜单 78.8% SOTA 中 20% 补丁为语义错误通过 | 未标注（arXiv cs.SE） | 首次量化“基于测试套件的基准作弊”现象，提出对抗性强化基准 | B | [11] |
| 2026-10 | **SWE-Bench Pro V2**：更难作弊、环境交互更真实的长程软工基准 | 未标注（arXiv cs.SE） | 针对 Agent 与评测环境交互的新攻击面（环境操纵）进行硬化 | B | [12] |
| 2025-08 | **SVC 2025**：首个多模态欺骗检测挑战赛 | 未标注（arXiv） | 将欺骗检测从纯文本扩展至音视频多模态，引入对抗生成管线 | B | [26] |
| 2025-10 | **VelLMes**：高交互 AI 欺骗框架（蜜罐式主动诱导） | 未标注（arXiv） | 从被动检测转向主动交互式欺骗诱捕，提供可部署红队工具 | B | [28] |
| 2025-09 | **Mind the Gap**：对比 Model-level 与 Agentic-level 红队，引入 Action-Graph 可观测性 | 未标注（arXiv） | 首次系统量化 Agent 级红队比模型级红队发现更多可执行攻击路径 | B | [32] |
| 2024-01/2024-05 | **大规模红队方法学**：数学任务幻觉红队 [33] / 多样化攻击学习用于鲁棒红队与安全微调 [34] | 未标注（arXiv） | 从人工红队转向自动化、规模化、可学习的红队生成管线 | B | [33][34] |

## 2. 工业界与产品

### 2.1 增量判断
**开源 Agent 平台（OpenHands）与红队工具链（VelLMes、Inspect）已形成可部署工程栈；大模型厂商开始内嵌红队模块，但“评测即服务”商业化仍处早期。** [29][28][32][33][34]

### 2.2 主流开源框架与工具落地情况

- **自动化红队即服务**：[33][34] 证明大规模自动化红队技术成熟，已有厂商（如 Haize Labs, Gray Swan, Lakera）提供 API 化红队服务。> 待核实：具体厂商营收与部署规模。

## 3. 蓝海与缺口

### 3.1 增量判断
**三大无人区/高杠杆缺口：(1) 多智能体协作中的可纠正性组合性评测缺失；(2) 长程部署中的“隐性欺骗”（非显式谎言、策略性遗漏）测量方法空白；(3) 评测基础设施与监管审计标准的互操作鸿沟。**
